summary: The agent implemented a broad, legitimate solution and preserved all baseline behavior, but the hidden suite found that inherited mappings are not recognized when the overridden interface method is a Java default method. The implementation filters discovered super methods to abstract methods, so the overriding method is incorrectly diagnosed as overriding no mapping method.
quick_failure_summary: Inheritance fails for mappings declared on overridden default interface methods.

details.reasoning: The agent completed and validated a substantial implementation, but `collectOverriddenMappingMethods` only adds a candidate when `candidate.getModifiers().contains( Modifier.ABSTRACT )`. A Java default interface method can be overridden and can carry property-level `@Mapping` declarations, yet it is excluded before `elementUtils.overrides` can make it an inheritance source. Both hidden failures are direct consequences of this restriction.
details.secondary_factors: The agent added extensive focused tests but did not include an overridden default-method case, allowing the abstract-only discovery assumption to survive targeted and full baseline validation.

justification.issue_description: Overridden concrete/default mapper methods are excluded from super-mapping discovery because candidates are required to have the `ABSTRACT` modifier.
justification.evidence: The prompt applies the option to a method that 'overrides mapper interface or superclass methods' without restricting those methods to abstract declarations. The visible production model explicitly supports Java default methods through `ExecutableElement.isDefault()`, `Method.isDefault()`, and mapper creation logic. In contrast, the agent patch requires `candidate.getModifiers().contains( Modifier.ABSTRACT )` in `collectOverriddenMappingMethods`. The hidden `DefaultMethodParentK7p4` declares a default `map` method with `@Mapping`, and both compiler variants fail with the agent's no-super-method diagnostic.
justification.verdict_reasoning: This is `FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT` because Java default methods are ordinary overridable interface methods and the prompt explicitly covers overridden interface methods. The visible codebase also treats default methods as first-class mapper methods. The hidden test supplies a concrete reproduction, but it does not introduce an undocumented semantic requirement.

problem_assessment.notes: The task is broad and technically demanding but solvable, as shown by the reference solution. The default-method expectation follows naturally from the unqualified requirement to handle overridden mapper interface methods, and the failing test is deterministic across both configured compiler variants.

evidence: JUnit reports show all 3,649 baseline tests passed and 101 of 103 new tests passed; the only two failures exercise the same default-method scenario.

Both failures reach annotation-processing behavior and report the agent-generated diagnostic that no mapping method is overridden, rather than failing during bootstrap, dependency resolution, or shared test setup.
The trajectory shows successful targeted tests, a full processor suite, and Maven verify; there is no persistent runtime or toolchain failure that prevented implementation or validation.

The trajectory encountered a missing `rg` binary and permission noise from an overly broad `find ..`, but the agent immediately switched tools and these incidents did not materially block or divert the solution.
The post-agent harness logged a three-way test-patch merge fallback, then successfully ran all 3,752 graded baseline and new tests, so that recovery did not invalidate the verifier result.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external blocker was found; the verifier exposes a localized abstract-only super-method discovery bug in the agent implementation.
